title: Admin contact-submission routes have no authentication (5 routes)
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/contact-submission/contact-submission.admin.routes.js:1-14`
**Root Cause:** All five admin routes (`GET /`, `GET /stats`, `GET /:id`, `PATCH /:id`, `DELETE /:id`) at `/api/admin/contact-submissions` have no `authenticate` or `requirePermission` middleware. The routes expose PII (names, emails, phone numbers, IP addresses) of all contact form submitters without requiring any credentials.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `contact-submission.admin.routes.js`, import `authenticate` from the auth middleware and `requirePermission` from the RBAC middleware. Add both as preHandlers to all 5 routes: `router.get('/', authenticate, requirePermission('admin.read'), controller.list)`. Apply the same pattern to `/stats`, `/:id` GET, `/:id` PATCH, and `/:id` DELETE.
fixEvidence: CWE-306 / OWASP A01 — contact-submission.admin.routes.js:1-14 — GET/GET-stats/GET-id/PATCH/DELETE all unprotected

title: Newsletter admin routes expose subscriber list without authentication
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/newsletter/newsletter.admin.routes.js:1-11`
**Root Cause:** `GET /api/admin/newsletter` (list all subscribers) and `DELETE /api/admin/newsletter/:id` have no `authenticate` or `requirePermission` middleware. Email subscriber lists and subscriber metadata are fully exposed without credentials — an unauthenticated attacker can enumerate all newsletter subscribers and delete subscription records.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `newsletter.admin.routes.js`, add `authenticate` and `requirePermission('admin.read')` as preHandlers to all route definitions. For the DELETE route, use `requirePermission('admin.delete')`. Same pattern as other admin route files in the project.
fixEvidence: CWE-306 / OWASP A01 — newsletter.admin.routes.js:1-11 — subscriber emails/IDs publicly enumerable

title: Keycloak JWKS failure silently falls back to HS256 with dev secret
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/authenticate.js:46-53`
**Root Cause:** When Keycloak JWKS verification fails for any reason (network timeout, misconfiguration), the code falls back to `jwt.verify(token, JWT_SECRET)` where `JWT_SECRET` has the value `dev_jwt_secret_key` (committed in `.env`). An attacker who knows this well-known dev secret (or reads the committed `.env`) can self-issue HS256 tokens and fully impersonate any user — including those with SUPERADMIN roles.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/authenticate.js`, delete the `try/catch` fallback block (lines 46-53) that calls `jwt.verify(token, JWT_SECRET)`. After the JWKS verification block, if verification fails for any reason, throw a 401 immediately: `return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Authentication failed' })`. There must be no local JWT fallback path. Also remove `JWT_SECRET` from the codebase as it is no longer needed.
fixEvidence: CWE-327 / OWASP A02 — authenticate.js:46-53 — JWT_SECRET='dev_jwt_secret_key'; attacker issues HS256 tokens

title: Policy bulkOperation runs updateMany without organizationId filter
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/policy.repository.js`
**Root Cause:** `PolicyRepository.bulkOperation()` runs `Policy.updateMany({ policyId: { $in: policyIds } })` with no `organizationId` filter. An authenticated user from Organization A can supply policy IDs belonging to Organization B, successfully archiving or deleting them. The controller passes user-supplied IDs directly without cross-referencing the caller's org.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Update `PolicyRepository.bulkOperation(policyIds, action, userId)` to accept `orgId` as a required parameter. Add `organizationId: orgId` to both the `Policy.updateMany` filter and any `Policy.find` calls within the method. Update the controller call site to pass `req.user.organizationId` (or `req.orgId`). Add an assertion that `orgId` is non-null before executing.
fixEvidence: CWE-639 / OWASP A01 — policy.repository.js — Org A can archive/delete Org B policies

title: Policy export job status fetched without organizationId verification
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/policy.service.js`
**Root Cause:** `GET /api/policies/export/download?jobId=` fetches a BullMQ job by caller-supplied `jobId` without verifying that the job's `orgId` matches the requesting user's `organizationId`. Any authenticated user who can guess or enumerate a valid `jobId` (UUID-based, but finite space) can retrieve another organization's policy export presigned S3 URL.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `policy.service.js` `getExportStatus()`, after retrieving the job add: `if (!job || job.data.orgId !== req.user.organizationId) { throw new ForbiddenError('Access denied'); }` before returning any job data. Add this check before any data is extracted from the job object.
fixEvidence: CWE-639 / OWASP A01 — policy.service.js — any authenticated user retrieves any org's export URL

title: GET /notebooks/{id} endpoint has no authentication dependency
description:
**Files:** `python-notebookAI-service/routers/notebooks.py:92-99`
**Root Cause:** The `GET /api/v1/notebooks/{notebook_id}` endpoint has no `Depends(verify_token)` dependency, while the adjacent `GET /api/v1/notebooks/assessment/{assessment_id}` endpoint does require authentication. Any unauthenticated caller with a valid-looking MongoDB ObjectId can retrieve any notebook record, including AI analysis results from any organization.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add `user_info: Dict = Depends(verify_token)` as a parameter to the `GET /api/v1/notebooks/{notebook_id}` handler in `python-notebookAI-service/routers/notebooks.py`. Add `organizationId: user_info.get('organizationId')` to the `find_one` query to enforce tenant scoping. Verify all other notebook endpoints similarly have auth dependencies.
fixEvidence: CWE-306 / OWASP A01 — notebooks.py:92-99 — adjacent endpoint has auth; this one does not

title: Next.js middleware returns next() for ALL /api/ routes — bypasses auth check
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/middleware.js:30`
**Root Cause:** The Next.js middleware explicitly returns `NextResponse.next()` for every request whose path starts with `/api/`, meaning no authentication check is performed for any Next.js API route. Any API route handler that does not implement its own session check is therefore publicly accessible. This contradicts the assumption that the middleware provides a security layer for all private routes.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `vibrantix-client-panel/src/middleware.js`, narrow the early return for `/api/` paths. Replace: `if (pathname.startsWith('/api/')) return NextResponse.next();` with: `if (pathname.startsWith('/api/auth/')) return NextResponse.next();`. For all other `/api/` routes, let the standard authentication check proceed. Audit all `/app/api/` route handlers to confirm they check session via `getServerSession()`.
fixEvidence: CWE-306 / CWE-284 / OWASP A01 — middleware.js:30 — any unauthenticated /api/ handler without own auth check is public

title: Notebook assessment query missing organizationId scoping
description:
**Files:** `python-notebookAI-service/routers/notebooks.py:60-70`
**Root Cause:** `GET /api/v1/notebooks/assessment/{assessment_id}` performs `db.notebook_output.find_one({'assessment_id': assessment_id})` with no `organizationId` filter. An authenticated user from Organization A can retrieve Organization B's notebook outputs by supplying a known or guessed `assessment_id` value, constituting a cross-tenant IDOR.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `python-notebookAI-service/routers/notebooks.py` at the assessment notebook endpoint (lines 60-70), update the `find_one` query to: `db.notebook_output.find_one({'assessment_id': assessment_id, 'organizationId': user_info.get('organizationId')})`. Apply the same `organizationId` filter to every other MongoDB query in this file and verify all other service routers have consistent org scoping.
fixEvidence: CWE-639 / OWASP A01 — notebooks.py:60-70 — Org A retrieves Org B notebooks by guessing assessment_id
